item: Which text gives the judge a general power to attempt conciliation between the parties at any stage of the proceedings (CPCA general provisions, and the chapter on conciliation, about articles 990 and following)?
May the parties reconcile on their own initiative, and may the judge propose it at any stage, in any matter not touching public order?
Where and when is the conciliation attempt held (the place and time fixed by the judge), and is it attempted by the judge himself?
What form does a conciliation record take (signed by the parties, the judge and the clerk, filed at the registry) and what force does it have (an executory title)?
Is the judge obliged to propose mediation to the parties, and in which matters (all matters except family matters, labour matters and anything that may touch public order)?
When is mediation proposed (at the first hearing) and must the parties accept it (it needs their agreement)?
Who may be appointed as mediator (a natural person or an association), and what conditions must the mediator meet?
Does mediation cover the whole dispute or may it cover part of it; does the judge stay seized and may he take any measure he thinks necessary during it?
How long may mediation last (three months at most) and may it be extended (once, for the same period, at the mediator's request and with the parties' agreement)?
Is the order appointing the mediator open to appeal (it is not), and what must it contain (the parties' consent, the mediator's mission, the period, the date the case returns)?
May the judge end the mediation at any time, of his own motion or at the request of the mediator or a party, when it appears impossible to proceed properly?
Is the mediator bound to confidentiality toward third parties, and can what was said in mediation be used later?

What happens at the end of mediation: written report by the mediator, an agreement signed by the parties and the mediator, its approval by an order of the judge not open to any appeal, and its force as an executory title?
What happens when mediation fails: the case returns to the roll and proceeds?
Family matters: are the conciliation attempts mandatory before a judgment of divorce (Family Code 49, as amended in 2005, and the CPCA chapter on divorce, about articles 439 and following)?
Family matters: within what period must the attempts be made (several attempts within at most three months from the filing of the claim)?
Family matters: are the attempts held in chambers, with the spouses heard separately and then together, and may a family member attend at the spouses' request?

Family matters: what if a spouse fails to attend: a legitimate excuse lets the judge set another date or delegate a judge; an unexcused absence of the plaintiff, or of the defendant summoned in person, leads to a record and the case proceeds?
Family matters: may the judge grant the spouses a period of reflection, and how long (up to three months)?
Family matters: when the spouses reconcile, is a record drawn up and does it have executory force?
Family matters: do the attempts apply to every form of dissolution (divorce at the husband's will, by mutual consent, tatliq at the wife's request, khul)?

Family matters: when the dispute between the spouses worsens and the harm is not proven, must the judge appoint two arbiters, one from each family, who report within two months (Family Code 56; CPCA articles on arbiters, about 446 and 447)?
Family matters: is mediation excluded for family matters, and conciliation the only route?
Specialised commercial court: must the claim be preceded by a conciliation attempt under penalty of inadmissibility (CPCA 536 bis 4 and following, added by Law 22-13 of 2022)?
Specialised commercial court: before whom is the conciliation held (the president of the court or a judge he designates), how is it requested, and how long does it last (about three months)?
Specialised commercial court: what document proves the failed attempt (a record of non-conciliation) and must it be attached to the petition?
Specialised commercial court: is the inadmissibility raised by the court of its own motion, and is it of public order?
Specialised commercial court: does a conciliation agreement reached there have executory force once approved?

Which matters fall under the specialised commercial court (to know when the prior conciliation applies): intellectual property, commercial companies, judicial settlement and bankruptcy, banks with traders, maritime and air transport and insurance, international trade (import ordinary-court-exits)?
Ordinary commercial disputes before the commercial section of an ordinary court: is there any mandatory prior conciliation (no), only the general optional one and mandatory proposal of mediation?

Labour disputes: the prior conciliation before the labour inspection's conciliation office is a different procedure (Law 90-04) and belongs to labour-prelitigation; mediation is excluded in labour matters.
Administrative courts: conciliation in full-jurisdiction administrative cases is a separate procedure (CPCA articles about 970 to 974) and is not this module.
Arbitration (CPCA articles from about 1006) looks like an alternative route but is a separate procedure.
Does a pending mediation or conciliation suspend or interrupt any limitation or forfeiture period (look for a text; otherwise import periods and warn)?
Does the petition itself need to mention the conciliation or mediation (only the record of non-conciliation before the specialised commercial court)?
Amendments to remember: Ordinance 05-02 amending Family Code 49; Law 22-13 adding the specialised commercial court and its prior conciliation; any later amendment of the CPCA.
Does the court have a general duty to attempt conciliation between the parties in civil matters, and at what stage may it do so?
Can the parties ask for conciliation themselves, at any stage of the case, and who records the outcome?
What is the legal force of a record of conciliation signed before the judge (is it an enforceable title)?
Is conciliation obligatory in divorce matters, and must the judge attempt it before ruling?
How many conciliation sessions must the judge hold in a divorce petition and within what period?
How long may the conciliation attempts last in a divorce case, and may the judge extend them?
Must the spouses appear in person for the conciliation session, and may a representative attend?
Does the public prosecutor have to be informed or attend in family matters, and what is the effect of his absence?
Is the record of the conciliation attempt in a divorce case mandatory, and what does the lack of it cost the judgment?
May the judge order a provisional measure (custody, maintenance, housing, visitation) during the conciliation period?
Does the Family Code require the judge to attempt reconciliation before pronouncing a divorce by judicial decision?
Is conciliation required before the specialised commercial court, and for which disputes?
What is the effect on the claim of not attempting conciliation before the specialised commercial court (inadmissibility, stay)?
Who conducts the conciliation before the specialised commercial court, and within what time?
Does the conciliation before the specialised commercial court suspend limitation or time limits?
What is the judicial mediation (mediation by a mediator appointed by the judge) and in what matters may it be proposed?
Does the judge need the parties' consent to order mediation, and may a party refuse?
How long does a mediation last, and may it be renewed once?
Who may be appointed as mediator, and how is the mediator paid (deposit, fees)?
What does the mediator report to the judge, and what is the effect of the agreement the parties reach?
Is mediation excluded in some matters (family status, public order, matters involving the State)?
Does the mediation suspend the proceedings and does it suspend limitation periods?
Is what is said during mediation confidential and may it be used before the court afterwards?
How is the agreement reached in mediation made enforceable (approval by the judge, record, order)?
What happens if the mediation fails: does the case simply resume, and who sets the next hearing?
Is labour conciliation before the conciliation office a separate matter handled by another module?
Does conciliation in other matters (neighbour, tenancy, small claims) exist as a mandatory step?
What does the lawyer state in the petition about earlier conciliation attempts?
What is the position when one spouse resides abroad: can conciliation be done in absence?
Do the rules on conciliation differ between divorce at the request of one spouse, by mutual consent, tatliq and khul?
